title: Salvation! What a Glorious Plan
description: Salvation! What a Glorious Plan in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 6 verses and a piano.
about: John Newton wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book III, hymn 85, “Salvation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sal-va-tion! what a glo-rious plan, How suit-ed to our need! The grace that rais-es fall-en man, Is won-der-ful in-deed!

lines: The grace that raises fallen man,
Truth, Wisdom, Justice, Pow'r and Love,
When Jesus left the courts above,
And died to save his own.
Truth, Wisdom, Justice, Pow'r and Love,
And yet the sinner lives by faith,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: John Newton died in 1807.
credits: Words by John Newton (1725–1807), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
